A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DecepGPT research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and content relocation.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, cross-domain and cross-cultural experiments, component ablations, and human auditing of 100 model outputs.

after.justification: v4 reports original detection experiments, ablations, and human audits, including additional Real-Life Trials results and annotation-agreement measurement.

M1.justification: The SICS gating and polarity refinement, DMC distillation, report-generation schema, and joint loss are retained. The corrected bias in Equation (1) matches the parameters already described in v3 and does not establish a changed implementation.

E1.justification: v4 adds actual evaluation on Real-Life Trials in Appendix 2; v3 only includes that dataset in comparative statistics. This extends evaluated coverage from laboratory and game-show scenarios to courtroom false testimony, a substantive new application domain. The existing deception benchmarks and four T4 cultures remain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the retained experiments. The new courtroom evaluation uses LieNet, PECL, and AFFAKT, all already evaluated in v3, extending existing comparison methods to the additional benchmark.

E3.justification: v4 adds single-component SICS control configurations and corrects Germany's Section 4.2 sample count from 760 to 702, matching both versions' Table 1. Existing folds and fine-tuning budgets remain unchanged. Section 4.1 replaces the explicit separate-backbone/MER2024 initialization account with a pretrained-AffectGPT description; this does not establish reruns. The new RLT split protocol is unspecified.

E4.justification: v4 Table 7 adds tests of the global prior, polarity adjustment, and gating individually, extending v3's leave-one-component-out analysis. The paired-component entries reproduce the earlier removal experiments. Qualitative report excerpts are revised in appendix Figure 3; existing cross-domain ablations, representation analyses, and quantitative audits are retained.

E5.justification: Section 3.1 newly reports chance-corrected annotation agreement: Cohen's kappa is 0.73 for discrete cue/reasoning labels, with two annotators and three calibration rounds disclosed. This adds annotation-reliability estimation, without introducing model-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New results include RLT accuracy/F1 of 87.82/88.54, versus AFFAKT's 86.70/87.60, and single-component SICS accuracies of 68.45, 68.81, and 68.62. Annotation agreement and revised qualitative excerpts are also added. Existing benchmark, transfer, cultural, and report-quality scores remain unchanged; v3 Table D1 becomes v4 main-text Table 3.

T1.justification: Equation (1) corrects the residual definition's final additive term from W2 to the bias b2, resolving its inconsistency with the declared parameters. The remaining mathematical formulation is retained, with no added theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same three central contributions: structured reasoning supervision, T4-Deception, and SICS/DMC. The abstract retains the claims of state-of-the-art detection and cross-domain/cultural transferability. The rewritten conclusion does not materially redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: Related Work replaces the strong assertion that SICS explicitly decouples persona noise with a more restrained explanation of joint representation stabilization. The new RLT discussion extends the applicability interpretation to less-controlled courtroom scenarios. Existing cross-cultural and modality-balancing interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: v4 replaces the promised full release with a code/data repository link and adds clip-selection rules, label verification, the 0.9-second minimum duration, annotator calibration, and expanded GPT-4o role descriptions. Conversely, it removes explicit backbone names, MER2024 alignment details, and Appendix D.1's metric explanations and GPT-Score scale. These materially change reproducibility documentation; linked resources were not externally verified.

R1.justification: v4 adds an MLLM Reasoning subsection citing Video-ChatGPT and multimodal chain-of-thought work, plus recent deception, domain-adaptation, and micro-gesture references. It removes several references, including Domain Separation Networks and the earlier hallucination-audit citations. This extends and refines positioning while retaining the same central research context.

P1.justification: Related Work, the method overview, dataset description, and conclusion receive targeted rewrites and grammatical corrections. Report-quality discussion moves into the main text, appendices are reorganized, and affiliations and acknowledgements are expanded. The main section sequence and most technical exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 substantially changes page geometry, text width, exhibit sizing, and placement throughout. Figure 1 is redrawn; the SICS component table is expanded and transposed; subject counts move from appendix Figure A3 into Table 1. The linguistic-results table moves into the main text, and the revised qualitative figure moves into the appendix.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly strengthens the paper through courtroom evidence, more informative component ablations, annotation-agreement reporting, and concrete dataset-construction details. It also corrects Equation (1) and provides code/data access information. These gains are limited by omitted pretraining and scoring details and the unspecified RLT evaluation protocol. The central method and established benchmark results remain unchanged.
